title: Constraint sandboxing for toolcall delimiters and subtoken rewrites
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Improves structured output robustness: isolates constrained-decoding backends into a sandboxed facade to avoid cross-backend contamination; fixes streaming function-call delimiter handling when tokens split across chunks; introduces a subtoken rewrite pass to preserve escape sequences in toolcall payloads.
body:
Motivation:
Large structured outputs (JSON + toolcall frames) surfaced a couple of production issues: (1) regex/CFG backends occasionally leaked internal parser state across subsequent requests when run in the same worker process under certain memory reuse patterns; (2) streaming responses that produced function/toolcall frames could split delimiter tokens across stream chunks, causing the OpenAI-compat shim to mis-detect function boundaries and emit malformed partial toolcall payloads; (3) tokenizer subtokenization of escape sequences (e.g., backslashes and quotes inside serialized JSON) sometimes produced rewrite sequences that the constrained decoders did not re-assemble correctly, resulting in invalid JSON or broken toolcall args.

This PR introduces a combination of runtime and API-surface changes to address these problems with minimal disruption: a lightweight "constraint sandbox" facade that executes grammar/CFG and regex-based constraint backends in isolated execution contexts (clearing parser/KV state between requests), a streaming boundary reconciler in the OpenAI-compat streaming shim that buffers incomplete delimiter subtokens and replays them into the decoder, and a tokenizer subtoken rewrite pass that normalizes escape sequences before constraint checking and after final token assembly.

Summary of changes:
- New runtime facet: constraint_sandbox (redwood/runtime/constraint_sandbox.rs) — isolates backend state and exposes a thin facade compatible with the existing constraint orchestrator API. Sandboxing is opt-in via an environment flag and defaults to enabled for hosted and dedicated environments.
- Streaming shim updates (redwood/compat/openai/stream_shim.py): implement boundary reconstructor to handle delimiters split across chunks; adds adaptive buffering thresholds to avoid undue latency.
- Subtoken rewrite pass (redwood/tokenizer/subtoken_rewriter.py): canonicalizes common escape patterns, preserves backslash-quote pairs across subtoken boundaries, and exposes hooks for constraint backends to run post-rewrite.
- Toolcall framing handler improvements (redwood/api/handlers/toolcall_stream.py): makes detection of function call start/end tolerant to subtoken boundary artifacts and adds a validation fallback that emits an explicit partial-frame marker in streaming events when we cannot confidently finish a frame.
- Tests and fuzzing: new fuzz harness for streamed toolcall framing, unit tests covering CFG and regex backends under sandboxing, and a regression test for a previously observed incident where a leaked parser state produced stale anchors.

Checklist:
- [x] Sandbox facade implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Streaming boundary reconstructor implemented and integration tested against the OpenAI-compat shim
- [x] Subtoken rewrite pass covered by unit tests and deterministic examples
- [x] Added regression test reproducing the leaky-state scenario
- [x] CI passes (lint, unit, integration, fuzz)
- [x] Release note entry drafted

Compatibility notes:
- API surface unchanged; sandboxing is internal and backward-compatible.
- Opt-out flag: REDWOOD_CONSTRAINT_SANDBOX=0 will preserve previous behavior for a short compatibility window.

Operational notes:
- Rollout plan: enable sandboxing in staging immediately; monitor p95 latency and streamed event drops for 72h; enable in production by percentage rollout. The sandbox adds a small allocation/teardown cost in the constrained backends path (measured ~0.7% p95 token latency increase in microbenchmarks on CPU-bound regex-heavy workloads).

Why not other approaches?
- We evaluated full process isolation (per-request subprocess) but that had too high of a throughput/socket cost. The chosen sandbox provides memory and state isolation with minimal IPC overhead.

Please see the commits below for implementation details and the tests directory for reproducer scripts.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can you measure the p99 memory impact for the sandbox lifecycle? In initial run the heap baseline grew ~3% on small workers. -- replied: added microbench and measurement in perf_benchmarks section, heap delta ~+2.1% p99 for heavy regex workloads.

Marta Ruiz: The streaming buffer threshold could exacerbate tail latency under high concurrency. Suggest adaptive ceiling and tests. -- replied: implemented adaptive ceiling with backpressure hook and added concurrency test in tests/fuzz.

Liam Chen: We should not mutate token text in-place before constraint backends run; prefer rewrite pass that returns canonicalized text. -- replied: refactored to make rewrite pass pure and add a copy-on-write fast path; added docs to tokenizer API.
Marta Ruiz: Please add an opt-out env to help narrowblast while rolling. -- replied: added REDWOOD_CONSTRAINT_SANDBOX env flag and documented rollout steps.
testing_summary: Unit tests: 42 new tests (tokenizer, sandbox, framing). Integration: streaming-compatible harness run against the OpenAI-compat shim with 10k simulated streaming events; all assertions passed. Fuzz: added harness discovered two edge cases (both fixed in subsequent commits). CI: full pipeline passing after one rerun of flaky stream-emitter test.
perf_benchmarks: Microbench on c5.large-equivalent: baseline (no sandbox) p95 token latency: 12.1ms; with sandbox enabled p95: 12.2ms (+0.8%). Heavy regex workload p95 delta: ~0.7-1.3% depending on pattern complexity. Memory p99 delta: +2.1% for extreme regex cases; normal workloads show <0.5% change.
security_notes: No secrets or keys are added. The sandbox reduces risk of state leak between requests; added unit tests to assert zero-cross-request state retention for constraint backends.
incident_linkage: Related to SUP-411 incident where a streaming toolcall produced malformed JSON leading to a retry storm; regression test reproduces the sequence and is included.
notes_for_release: Enable by default in hosted and dedicated; private deployments can opt-in via REDWOOD_CONSTRAINT_SANDBOX=1. Watch the streaming_event_error rate and p95 latency for the first 48 hours after rollout.
changelog_entry: Fix: sandbox constraint backends to prevent parser state leakage and improve streaming toolcall framing robustness (Priya Kapoor)
